extracted.intended_audience: public relations students and practitioners writing press releases and doing media relations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and pitching effective press releases: required components, quality criteria (newsworthiness, clarity, AP style), release types, pitching tactics, audience tailoring, and common pitfalls to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letterhead/identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include organizational letterhead or other identifying information on the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides source credibility and immediate identification for journalists; typically at the top of the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information at top
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact information at the top of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, phone, email (and possibly cell) so reporters can easily reach a spokesperson or media contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release date / "FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE"
rubrics_metrics.description: State the release date and use notation such as "FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE" when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies timing expectations for publication; alternatively indicate an embargo date/time if not immediate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline (centered, bold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a centered, bold headline to summarize the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline should be attention-getting and concise, signaling the key angle to editors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline + lead paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a dateline (city, date) followed immediately by a lead paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead should answer the essential who/what/when/where/why/how and 'carry the story' so readers grasp the news quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body in inverted pyramid
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the body using the inverted pyramid: most important information first, followed by supporting details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates editorial trimming and ensures core facts remain if copy is shortened; use short paragraphs and clear transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness — Real news, not promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the release presents a genuine news angle (impact, timeliness, relevance) rather than marketing puffery; evaluate why a journalist's audience should care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy — Verifiable facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All facts, names, dates, numbers, and quotations must be checked and verifiable to avoid retractions and loss of credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity — 1-2 pages preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep releases concise; editors prefer succinct copy that can be quickly scanned and easily trimmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity — Simple, direct language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon and marketing-speak; use plain language and active voice so the main point is immediately understandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Style — AP style throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Associated Press style conventions for consistency and to meet newsroom expectations (dates, numbers, titles, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format
rubrics_metrics.description: Format — Standard formatting expected by media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conventional layout (letterhead, dateline, lead, boilerplate) and readable fonts/spacing so the release appears professional to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement (release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcement — Personnel, mergers, acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the announcement format for formal organizational news that has intrinsic informational value to reporters and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spot news (release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spot news — Breaking events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For immediate, time-sensitive events; leads should emphasize timeliness and essential facts for rapid reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaction (release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reaction — Response to external events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a timely, clear stance and supporting information; anticipate media questions and provide contact/quote for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad news (release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bad news — Crisis, scandal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use crisis communications principles: be factual, timely, transparent where possible, and provide steps being taken; avoid spin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local news (release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local news — Community-relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize local angle, impacts, names, and places to increase pickup by community outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature (release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature — Soft news, human interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use storytelling techniques, quotes, and color; less urgency than spot news but still must fit outlet tone/format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customize to outlet/journalist (pitching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Customize pitches and releases to the specific outlet and journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference the reporter's beat, past coverage, and audience; show why the story is a good fit rather than sending generic copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send only to relevant beats (pitching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Send releases only to journalists covering relevant beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeting increases likelihood of pickup and reduces annoyance; avoid blasting unrelated reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up appropriately (not aggressively) (pitching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow up with reporters appropriately but avoid aggressive persistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely, polite follow-up is recommended; excessive calls/emails harm relationships and reduce future responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build relationships (pitching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Build ongoing relationships with reporters and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term rapport improves placement and understanding of what an outlet values; reciprocity and respect are key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify primary audience (audience-centered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the primary audience (publics) for the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify who should receive and act on the information so messaging and angle align with audience needs and interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor message to publics (audience-centered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor the message to the identified publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust tone, detail, and emphasis to match the information needs and language of each target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple versions for different segments (audience-centered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare multiple versions of the release for different audience segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create shortened/expanded or localized variants for media, stakeholders, and niche audiences as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localize where possible (audience-centered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Localize content where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add local statistics, names, or impacts to increase relevance for regional outlets and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid burying the lead (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Burying the lead is a common mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the most newsworthy information in the lead; failure to do so reduces chances of pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using marketing-speak (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using marketing-speak (promotional language) is inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releases should read like news, not advertising; journalists edit out overt promotional wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic quotes (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Including generic, boilerplate quotes is a pitfall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific, attributable quotes that add insight or context rather than platitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid missing contact info (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing contact info undermines utility of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include clear media contact details to enable follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wrong format (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the wrong format harms credibility and usability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow standard press-release conventions (headline, dateline, lead, boilerplate) to meet newsroom expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wrong outlet targeting (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeting the wrong outlets reduces chances of pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research which outlets cover the topic and tailor distribution lists accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sending too early or too late (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor timing (too early or too late) can prevent coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider editorial calendars, embargoes, and reporters' deadlines when scheduling distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid following up too aggressively (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive follow-up is counterproductive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measured, respectful follow-ups; persistent harassment damages relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid not having a clear angle (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to present a clear news angle is a common error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and emphasize the most newsworthy element to make the release compelling to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid including untested claims (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Including unverified or untested claims is risky.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stick to verifiable facts; untested claims can lead to corrections and reputational harm.
